name: District of Columbia

agency.name: District of Columbia Department of Motor Vehicles

gaps: The excise tax rate of a gasoline, hybrid or plug-in hybrid car depends on its city MPG (EPA rating, rounded down), which the form does not ask; the engine shows the official range of the car's weight class, from the 40-MPG-or-more rate to the 20-MPG-or-less rate. Electric cars have one rate per weight class and are computed.

The excise tax is charged on the fair market value from the NADA guide for the Eastern region, not on the price; the engine applies the rate to the price typed. Many vehicles are exempt, and residents who received the DC earned income tax credit may pay the older 6%, 7% or 8% weight rates instead.
The summary rate of 6% is the excise rate of a 3,500 to 4,999 lb car rated 21 to 25 city MPG; actual rates run from 1% to 11%.
DC DMV lists a $30-a-year registration card fee among additional fees without saying that every registration pays it; it is shown as a range of $0 to $30.
Electric cars get a non-expiring inspection sticker; its price is not published on the fee page, so no inspection line is added for them.
No official DC page read for this release caps the dealer processing fee; type the dealer's figure.

summary.taxName: excise tax (1% to 11% by weight and MPG)
summary.docFeeNote: No cap read on an official DC page for this release; type the dealer's fee.
summary.inspectionWhere: Emissions inspection every two years at the DC inspection station, paid with the registration; brand-new cars get a four-year sticker and electric cars a non-expiring one.

singular: DC has no sales tax on cars: it charges an excise tax at titling, on the car's NADA fair market value [excise].
Since February 17, 2025, the excise rate depends on both unladen weight and city MPG, from 1% for a light electric car to 11% for a car of 5,000 lb or more rated 20 MPG or less [excise].
Electric cars lost their excise tax exemption in 2025 and now pay 1%, 2% or 3% depending on weight [excise].
Registration fees by weight rose on March 30, 2026: $70 a year up to 3,499 lb, $175 from 3,500 to 4,999 lb and $300 from 5,000 to 5,999 lb [reg-fees].
A brand-new battery electric car under 5,000 lb pays $40 a year for its first two registration years, then subtracts 1,000 lb from its weight to find its class [reg-fees].
The title fee rose to $30 on March 30, 2026, and each lien adds $20 [excise].
Inspection fees are collected with the registration: $10 for a new car's four-year sticker, then $35 every two years [inspection-fees].
Brand-new passenger cars are not taken through inspection, and fully electric passenger cars receive a non-expiring inspection sticker [inspections].
Since December 15, 2025, DC DMV adds a 2.5% service fee to every card payment [excise].
